EDIT:

And just for balance sake to all the good I've said about it in this and my replies below, here's some downsides to VR (at least the HTC Vive, Oculus Rift has even more imo):

  • It's bleeding edge and bloody expensive.
  • There's ultimately movement limitations and if you want to be truly exploratory in your game as a developer, you have to give the player an alternate form of movement in addition to whatever little play area they have. This can't be straight up movement with a directional pad cause you will give players serious motion sickness. This is probably the worst limitation. I wish I could have a much larger area and free roam in it without a cord hitting my back/legs. I'm not sure how to solve this, but I'm sure the next generation will bring at least wireless headsets which is a decent start. I've seen some demos where people have like an omni-directional treadmill thingy they walk on which seems kinda cool, but I can only imagine the price on hardware like that, and I'd suspect that support for it must be actively integrated into the game.
  • The setup is fairly intimidating for anyone not seriously technically inclined/committed to gaming in a big way.
  • The game selection overall is still kinda slim. Some of the experiences are amazingly fun, but there's arguably still lacking a killer app to sell the concept home for 90% of the people at its given barriers to entry.
  • While the motion controllers are everything the shitty kinect/wiimotes/etc. were meant to be and more (they do work amazingly flawlessly), I still wish I had something that was more like a glove at times or that the VR could just interpret what my hand was doing without any need for controllers.
  • Video lag can induce motion sickness, so performance is actually far more critical than in other games.
  • Text can be hard to read and the lens have to be perfectly over both eyes. If it gets off some from the headset shifting too much, things can be a bit blurry.
  • If you play for a long time, you'll get a little bit of neck fatigue.

So would I recommend everyone go out and buy one right now? Absolutely not. I can't see it being a good fit for anyone but the most technically obsessed and hardest core of gamers in its current state. I see it as something for early-adopters who will help the current companies refine and fund their future offerings. I firmly believe that with each generation of VR products, the answer to the question of "Is VR right for me?" will become increasingly yes for more people. I think that for a lot of people, if they had a friend who owned one or if there was a place they could try one out for a limited time (like a pay-to-play sorta deal), they'd love it.
